# ZeniPay

> ZeniPay (ZeniPay Inc., zenipay.ca) is a Canadian payment technology platform for small businesses and online stores. Businesses use it to send payment links and invoices, split an invoice into a deposit and 2 to 12 installments, and accept card and bank transfer payments. Card payments are processed by Finix, a PCI DSS Level 1 processor. ZeniPay is not a bank.

ZeniPay is part of Zeniva Group, founded by Alexandre Blais in Québec. Sister brands: Zeniva Travel (zenivatravel.com), ZeniCorp (zeniva.ca) and Zenitech (zenitech.dev). **ZeniPay is not ZenPay, Zen.com, Zenus Bank or Zenai Pay** — those are unrelated companies.

## Key facts

- Legal entity: ZeniPay Inc. (Canada), founded 2026, based in Québec
- Markets: Canada and the United States
- Currencies: invoices and payment links in CAD or USD; cards are charged in CAD (a USD amount shows the customer its CAD equivalent before paying)
- Payment methods: credit and debit cards (processed by Finix, PCI DSS Level 1, tokenized card fields) and bank transfers (EFT, up to $2,500 per transaction, 3 to 5 business days to settle)
- Languages: French and English
- Pricing: per-payment processing fees that depend on the business and payment type; ZeniPay does not publish generic rates — quotes on request at info@zeniva.ca
- Contact: info@zeniva.ca
- Founder: Alexandre Blais (https://zenipay.ca/alexandre-blais)

## What ZeniPay does

- [Payment links](https://zenipay.ca/paylinks) ([FR: lien de paiement](https://zenipay.ca/fr/lien-de-paiement)): amount, currency, description, optional expiry date, shareable URL and QR code; the customer pays without creating an account.
- [Online invoicing](https://zenipay.ca/invoices) ([FR: facturation en ligne](https://zenipay.ca/fr/facturation-en-ligne)): invoices emailed with a pay button; status moves to paid automatically; receipts sent to the customer.
- [Installment payments](https://zenipay.ca/installments) ([FR: paiement en versements](https://zenipay.ca/fr/paiement-en-versements)): 2 to 12 installments per invoice by amount or percentage; each installment has its own payment link and is emailed on its due date; reminders 3 and 7 days after an unpaid due date. ZeniPay does not lend money or charge customers interest.
- [Payment processing](https://zenipay.ca/payments) ([FR: processeur de paiement au Canada](https://zenipay.ca/fr/processeur-de-paiement-canada)): card and bank transfer payments by link, invoice or API.
- Orvel: the AI assistant inside the ZeniPay dashboard. It creates invoices, splits them into installments and sends payment links when asked in plain French or English, within the permissions the business grants; every action is logged.
- [Security](https://zenipay.ca/security): Finix PCI DSS Level 1 card processing, encryption in transit and at rest, signed sessions, tamper-evident audit trail.
- [Merchant program](https://zenipay.ca/merchant) and [developer docs](https://zenipay.ca/docs).

## Frequently asked

- Is ZeniPay a bank? No. It is a payment technology platform, not a bank or deposit-taking institution.
- Do customers need a ZeniPay account to pay? No. They open the link or invoice and pay by card or bank transfer.
- Can a business ask for a deposit? Yes: make the first installment due today; it is emailed immediately.

## Guides

Sourced guides (Revenu Québec, Canada Revenue Agency, Office de la protection du consommateur, FCAC, Justice Canada), checked 2026-10-02. Index: [FR](https://zenipay.ca/fr/guides) · [EN](https://zenipay.ca/guides)

- [Comment envoyer un lien de paiement à un client](https://zenipay.ca/fr/guides/envoyer-lien-de-paiement-client) ([EN: How to send a payment link](https://zenipay.ca/guides/how-to-send-a-payment-link)): 5 steps, channel by situation (email, text, QR), message template, avoiding phishing look-alikes, CASL s. 6(6) transactional exemption and s. 6(2) identification/unsubscribe requirements.
- [Facturer en ligne au Québec : TPS, TVQ et mentions obligatoires](https://zenipay.ca/fr/guides/facturer-en-ligne-quebec-tps-tvq) ([EN: Invoicing online in Québec: GST, QST](https://zenipay.ca/guides/quebec-invoicing-gst-qst)): GST 5% and QST 9.975% on the sale price, rounding, Revenu Québec required-information table (under $100, $100 to $499.99, $500+), $30,000 small-supplier threshold, French-language rule (Charter s. 57), six-year record retention.
- [Offrir le paiement en versements : options et pièges](https://zenipay.ca/fr/guides/offrir-paiement-en-versements) ([EN: Offering installment payments](https://zenipay.ca/guides/offering-installment-payments)): split invoice vs buy now pay later vs instalment sale, who carries the risk, when fees or a cash discount count as credit charges (OPC), sample 30/30/40 schedule.
